solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Something immune to challenge, customs-wise, landed aboard boat (6,3)

indicators.note: one thing goes on board, that is inside, the boat

blocks.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed boat
acred = owning land, as in the landed gentry

annotation.surface: Someone who owns land and lives on a boat seems to be beyond the reach of customs officers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Customs-wise' belongs to the definition: a sacred cow is untouchable by custom, not by the customs service. ACRED is an old word for owning acres.
annotation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is a custom or institution that nobody is allowed to question.

entries.clue: Caught half-a-dozen cats (5)

indicators.note: caught by the ear, that is heard

annotation.surface: Someone has trapped six cats.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cats' looks like a noun but is a verb: to cat is slang for to vomit, so it cats = it sicks.
annotation.definitionFit: To cat is British slang for to be sick, so cats means sicks.

entries.clue: Wake up, time for school — change, not having cold to get over (4,2,5,4)

indicators.note: the cold's letter is removed from the word for change

blocks.note: SWITCH without C (cold, as on a tap)

annotation.surface: A child is told to get up because school has started again, and must adjust to the change without having a cold as an excuse.
annotation.walkthrough: The dashes of the surface hide a plain charade: three pieces laid end to end, the last with one letter missing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain idiom: getting over a loss and accepting it are the same act.

entries.clue: Might I pass exam, scoring 50 per cent? See you at half-term (6,2)

indicators.note: only half the word counts
only half the word is used

blocks.note: CU is text-speak for see you
the first half of SEMESTER, a term

annotation.surface: A pupil worries about scraping through an exam and says goodbye until the half-term break.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Half-term' reads as the school holiday but splits into its parts: half of a word meaning term. A semester is an academic term, mostly in the US.
annotation.definitionFit: "Excuse me" is what you say when asking to squeeze past someone.

entries.clue: State where Congress banned a bicycle, bizarrely (8)

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a strange new way

annotation.surface: The US Congress has passed a strange law banning bicycles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' and 'Congress' pull toward American politics; here congress means sexual intercourse, and the state is a condition, not Ohio.
annotation.definitionFit: Celibacy is the condition of abstaining from sex, or congress.

entries.clue: Rugby score underpinning victory characteristic of season (6)

indicators.note: in a down answer, the piece that underpins sits below the other

blocks.note: a try is the main score in rugby

annotation.surface: A late try in rugby clinches a win typical of the season.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: wintry is characteristic of one season in particular, and the surface's sporting season is a misdirection.
annotation.definitionFit: Wintry describes things characteristic of winter, a season.

entries.clue: Person with plenty of time dismantled rifle (5)

indicators.note: taken apart and so rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone with time on their hands strips down a rifle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plenty of time' sounds like leisure; it is a prison sentence.
annotation.definitionFit: A lifer is a prisoner serving a life sentence, a person with plenty of time to do.

entries.clue: US cops on leave picked up devoted admirer (6)

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits on top of the second
in a down answer, lifting a word turns it upside down

annotation.surface: American police officers on leave collect a fan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts a homophone reading; in a down clue it means lift the word so it reads upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A lapdog is a person slavishly devoted to someone.

entries.clue: Force freedom in hearing where criminals once hung mischief-maker (15)

indicators.note: the word is taken as it is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: F is the symbol for force in physics

annotation.surface: A court hearing is forced on a trickster, with talk of freedom and of the old gallows.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the middle piece is a sound; F and GIBBET are spelt as usual.
annotation.definitionFit: A flibbertigibbet is a flighty, frivolous person; the name was once also given to an imp or mischief-maker.

entries.clue: Tie once more, going round course at which most won’t reach finish line? (5,4)

annotation.definition: at which most won’t reach finish line?
annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a description, standing for 'a race at which…'

indicators.note: RELACE goes round the course, and the course itself goes round: its first letter moves to the end

blocks.note: AYR, a Scottish racecourse, with its A cycled to the end

annotation.surface: Someone reties a shoelace on a course where most competitors never get to the end.
annotation.walkthrough: In a relay only the last runner of each team crosses the line, which is why most won't reach it. AYR is a racecourse town in Scotland.
annotation.definitionFit: In a relay race only the anchor runners finish, so most runners never reach the line.

entries.clue: Funny mineral found in mountain pass (7)

indicators.note: one piece is found inside the other

blocks.note: a col is a pass between peaks

annotation.surface: An odd mineral has turned up in a mountain pass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Funny' in the surface means strange; as the definition it means amusing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something comical makes you laugh, which is what funny means here.

entries.clue: Unplait curls for wedding (7)

indicators.note: the letters twist round into a new order

annotation.surface: A bride undoes her plaits and curls her hair for the wedding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Curls' reads as hair styling; it is telling the letters of UNPLAIT to twist into a new order.
annotation.definitionFit: Nuptial means relating to a wedding, as in nuptial vows.

entries.clue: Positions spectacles on one’s ears? (5)

indicators.note: the word as it falls on the ears, heard not seen

annotation.surface: Someone perches a pair of glasses on their ears.
annotation.walkthrough: Spectacles sit on the ears in the surface; here they are sights, and the ears are listening.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a site is the place where something is put, its position.

entries.clue: Altercation between boozer and son, a wheeler-dealer? (6,3)

indicators.note: the row sits between the pub and the son

blocks.note: a boozer is a pub, or bar

annotation.surface: A pub row between a drinker and a young man who likes to do deals.
annotation.walkthrough: A barrow boy is a British street trader selling from a handcart; the question mark marks the pun on the barrow's wheels.
annotation.definitionFit: A barrow boy deals goods from a wheeled barrow, so he is literally a wheeler-dealer.

entries.clue: Mother stopping in city destroyed close relationship (8)

indicators.note: the mother plugs the gap in the other letters
IN CITY is broken up and reassembled

annotation.surface: A mother has to stay put in a city that has been devastated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like the container indicator but belongs to the anagram fodder; 'stopping' does the enclosing job.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the closeness between lovers or friends.

entries.clue: It could be theft of internal post (6,3)

blocks.note: a crime carried out by someone on the staff
a post is a job, and internal means inside

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether things vanishing from the internal mail are being stolen.
annotation.walkthrough: The first reading is a crime committed by someone on the staff; the second is simply a job, or post, inside the firm.
annotation.definitionFit: An inside job is a theft by someone within the organisation, and it is also literally a post inside it.

entries.clue: Solo number from West Side Story missing intro (4)

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: "Maria" is a song from the musical West Side Story

annotation.surface: A solo song from West Side Story is performed without its introduction.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Solo number' is the definition, not the song being described; the song is Maria.
annotation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo piece for voice, in opera especially.

entries.clue: Monkey to stroll scratching tail in souk? (8)

indicators.note: the last letter is scratched off
one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a souk is an Arab market, or mart

annotation.surface: A monkey wanders through a market, scratching its tail.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a monkey scratching itself; 'scratching' means cutting off the end of MOSEY.
annotation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American monkey.

entries.clue: Vintage candle, perhaps one separated from candle-holder? (3,5)

blocks.note: a candle gives a flame; 'perhaps' flags the loose link

annotation.surface: An antique candle, perhaps one parted from its candlestick.
annotation.walkthrough: The candle-holder is not a candlestick but someone who still holds a candle for a former lover, and the old flame is that lover.
annotation.definitionFit: An old flame is a former lover; to hold a candle for someone is to still carry a torch for them.

entries.clue: Angry god from the east (4)

indicators.note: in an across answer, reading from the east means reading right to left

blocks.note: Eros, the Greek god of love

annotation.surface: A god arrives from the east in a temper.
annotation.walkthrough: Sore for angry is chiefly American usage, as in a sore loser.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use, chiefly American: to be sore at someone is to be cross with them.

entries.clue: Fix data set for digital manager (4,4)

blocks.note: a computer file is a set of data

annotation.surface: Correcting a dataset for someone who manages digital systems.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Digital' means relating to digits, that is fingers; the manager is what keeps fingernails in trim.
annotation.definitionFit: A nail file manages the nails on your digits, your fingers.

entries.clue: Trade union beset by enemies, one needing Labour in due course (6)

annotation.definition: one needing Labour in due course

indicators.note: surrounded on all sides by the enemies

annotation.surface: A trade union, surrounded by enemies, needs the Labour Party to come good eventually.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital L makes Labour look like the British political party; here it is childbirth, which the foetus will need at the due date.
annotation.definitionFit: A foetus awaits labour, the process of birth, when it is due.

entries.clue: Crown land regularly seized by parliament, but not last month (6)

indicators.note: 'regularly' means at regular intervals, so every other letter of LAND is taken
the letters are grabbed and held inside the other piece
'but not last' says the last letter of the parliament word is left out

blocks.note: DIET, a parliament, without its T
the second and fourth letters of LAND

annotation.surface: Crown lands are being taken over by parliament, though not last month.
annotation.walkthrough: A diet is a legislative assembly, as in Japan or historically in Germany. 'Crown land' reads as one phrase; 'Crown' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a diadem is the jewelled band worn by a monarch.

entries.clue: Dictatorship decides pot is malevolent to some extent (9)

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of 'decides' to the first letter of 'malevolent'

annotation.surface: A dictator decides that a drug is harmful, at least partly.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans four words, starting inside 'decides' and ending on the first letter of 'malevolent'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rule by a single absolute tyrant.

entries.clue: Trifle endlessly, frolicking (5)

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped
the letters play about into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone fools around endlessly, playing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trifle' does double duty: it is the definition and, cut short, the letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: To flirt is to trifle, to toy with someone's affections.

entries.clue: Reject scripture being brought up — it’s poisonous (5)

annotation.definitionNote: a clause standing for the noun: something poisonous

indicators.note: in a down answer, bringing up means lifting the letters so they read upwards

annotation.surface: Someone rejects a piece of scripture that is being quoted, calling it poison.
annotation.walkthrough: NIX and OT are joined and then the whole reversed, so OT ends up first.
annotation.definitionFit: A clause standing for the noun: a toxin is a poison made by a living organism.

entries.clue: Articulate sign up for series of talks (7)

blocks.note: TED is the conference series famous for its talks

annotation.surface: An eloquent speaker enrols in a lecture series.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' suggests eloquent; here it is the adjective meaning having joints, like an articulated lorry.
annotation.definitionFit: Articulate, in anatomy, means jointed, having joints.

entries.clue: Drama (TV) where politicians took a stand (7)

blocks.note: the box is slang for television

annotation.surface: A TV drama about where politicians made their stand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Took a stand' reads as adopting a position; literally, speakers once stood on a crate to address crowds.
annotation.definitionFit: A soapbox is the crate a public speaker stands on to harangue a crowd.

entries.clue: Stretch of forest habitat around bits of Thailand (5)

indicators.note: a stretch is only part of the text
the letters are read the other way round

annotation.surface: A stretch of forest habitat around parts of Thailand.
annotation.walkthrough: Read backwards through 'forest habitat' to find the answer. The baht is Thailand's currency.
annotation.definitionFit: Bahts are units of Thai currency, so bits of Thailand's money.

entries.clue: Shabby, dilapidated home: a tent (4-5)

indicators.note: falling to pieces, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone's shabby, run-down home turns out to be a tent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dilapidated' fits the surface as a description of the tent but is the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative use: clothes chewed by moths look worn, so anything tatty is so described.
